newsitem.title: QATAR: Mideast's $1.5 bln gas grid "inevitable" - planner.
newsitem.headline: Mideast's $1.5 bln gas grid "inevitable" - planner.

text.p: A $1.5 billion gas grid project connecting the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states is "inevitable", a promoter of the plan said on Tuesday.
"It is inevitable that we get it," Hassan Tayim from the GCC's Doha-based Gulf Organisation for Industrial Consulting (GOIC) told delegates at a gas conference in Qatar.

The 1,300 km pipeline, which would stretch from Kuwait to Oman, through Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, still needs approval in principle by GCC governments, an agreed tariff structure and private finance.
The project had an internal rate of return of 14-16 percent, Tayim told delegates.

GOIC's study on the phased development of the line, with a start-up in the early part of the next decade, is based on the need to meet rising gas demand, particularly in the UAE emirate of Dubai and Saudi Arabia.

GCC states had the potential to take 1.55 billion cubic feet a day from the proposed pipeline in the year 2000, rising to 2.25 billion cubic feet in 2010 and 3.8 billion cubic feet in 2020, Tayim said.
The future of the pipeline was questioned following a decision by Abu Dhabi to supply its fellow UAE emirate Dubai with natural gas, analysts said.
